findings.excerpt: ClassGroup.mulEquiv g (ClassGroup.mk0 P) = ClassGroup.mk0 (Ideal.mapNonZero g P)
findings.problem: This is the canonical computation rule for `ClassGroup.mulEquiv` on `mk0` classes, but it is not tagged @[simp]. Its companion `Ideal.coe_mapNonZero` is simp, and so is `clEnd_clProj`, which produces exactly the `ClassGroup.mulEquiv g (…mk0 P)` redex. As a result the file's own `clEnd_clProj_mk0` is proved by a manual two-step `rw` rather than `simp`. Downstream files also rewrite with it by name (e.g. `rw [w2kum_clAut_ofMul, ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk0, …]`, `rw [Φ₀, primeClass, ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk0, primeClass]`).
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The right side only introduces `mapNonZero`, which is already an opaque-but-simp-normalised constructor with `coe_mapNonZero`, so there is no loop. Then `clEnd_clProj_mk0` and `clGalAction_clProj_mk0` can be closed by `simp`, and the `rw [clEnd_clProj, ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk0]` chains become `simp`.
findings.benefit: The simp set can normalise `clEnd p g (clProj p R (ofMul (mk0 P)))` to `clProj … (mk0 (mapNonZero g P))` in one call. Users no longer need to remember a two-lemma `rw` sequence in each downstream proof.

findings.problem: `mulEquiv_refl_apply` and `mulEquiv_trans_apply` are functoriality rewrite rules (identity and composition collapse) but are plain theorems. They are only applied through `rw`, in `clEndHom` (lines 163 and 170) and in Def_NumberField_LevelArithmeticModP. The underlying identities on `Ideal.mapNonZero`, `map id = P` and `map (h∘g) = map h ∘ map g`, are proved inline with `show … from RingHom.ext …` and `Ideal.map_id` / `← Ideal.map_map`. They are not exposed as lemmas, so `simp` cannot normalise `mapNonZero (g.trans h) P` or `mapNonZero (RingEquiv.refl R) P` after `mulEquiv_mk0` fires.
findings.proposed_change: Extract `Ideal.mapNonZero_refl : Ideal.mapNonZero (RingEquiv.refl R) P = P` and `Ideal.mapNonZero_trans : Ideal.mapNonZero (g.trans h) P = Ideal.mapNonZero h (Ideal.mapNonZero g P)` from the inline proofs at lines 90–93 and 100–105, and tag them @[simp]. Also tag `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl_apply` and `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_trans_apply` as @[simp]. The trans lemma rewrites toward the composite of simpler maps, and the refl lemma strictly shrinks the term, so neither can cycle. The `Ideal.mapNonZero` identities are needed so that, if `mulEquiv_mk0` is simp, `simp` does not leave `mapNonZero (RingEquiv.refl R) P` or `mapNonZero (g.trans h) P` stuck.
findings.benefit: The proofs of `clEndHom.map_one'` and `map_mul'` and the corresponding proofs in the LevelArithmetic file can use `simp` instead of fragile `rw` ordering. Together with the `mulEquiv_mk0` simp lemma, the class-group action normalises coherently. The `mapNonZero` lemmas are also reusable by anyone working with that definition.
